section: Important contributors and contributions from different parts of the country
subsections: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution

accepted.s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’?
accepted.x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was popularly known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’ and was associated with the Khudai Khidmatgars.
accepted.tq: Use direct title–person recall.

accepted.s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ in connection with which event?
o: The Quit India Movement in Andhra
The boycott of the Simon Commission at Madras
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became known as ‘Andhra Kesari’ for his prominent role in the Simon boycott at Madras.
accepted.tq: Link the title with the specific event associated with its conferment.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Deshbandhu was the title of C.R. Das. Lala Lajpat Rai was known as Punjab Kesari or the Lion of Punjab.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped personality–title pair.

accepted.s: Sarojini Naidu was popularly known as which of the following?
accepted.x: Sarojini Naidu was popularly known as Bharat Kokila, or the Nightingale of India.
accepted.tq: Test a well-known title through direct recall.

accepted.s: The title ‘Sardar’ was associated with Vallabhbhai Patel after which event?
accepted.x: Vallabhbhai Patel came to be known as ‘Sardar’ after his leadership in the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.
accepted.tq: Use date-and-event discrimination for a title.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Punjab Kesari — Lala Lajpat Rai
2. Andhra Ratna — Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
3. Deshabhakta — Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
accepted.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was Punjab Kesari and Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was Andhra Ratna. Deshabhakta was Konda Venkatappayya, not Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
accepted.tq: Check each title–person pair before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: Who was known as ‘Desoddharaka’?
accepted.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was known as ‘Desoddharaka’ and was the founder of Andhra Patrika.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related Andhra titles and personalities.

accepted.s:
With reference to the titles and associated personalities, consider the following statements:
1. Mannathu Padmanabhan was known as Bharatha Kesari.
2. Mannathu Padmanabhan founded the Nair Service Society.
3. He was associated with the Vaikom and Guruvayur Satyagrahas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Mannathu Padmanabhan was associated with the title Bharatha Kesari, founded the NSS and participated in the Vaikom and Guruvayur Satyagrahas.
accepted.tq: Use a cluster of biographical statements and verify all three links.

accepted.s: Who called Gandhi ‘Mahatma’?
accepted.x: Rabindranath Tagore is associated with calling Gandhi ‘Mahatma’.
accepted.tq: Test the originator of a famous honorific.

accepted.s: ‘The Golden Threshold’ is associated with which author?
accepted.x: ‘The Golden Threshold’ was written by Sarojini Naidu.
accepted.tq: Distinguish literary works by their authors.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. The Discovery of India — Jawaharlal Nehru
2. Annihilation of Caste — B.R. Ambedkar
3. Sarvodaya — Mahatma Gandhi
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. The Discovery of India was written by Nehru, Annihilation of Caste by Ambedkar and Sarvodaya was Gandhi’s Gujarati rendering of Ruskin’s Unto This Last.
accepted.tq: Verify multiple work–author pairs and the associated literary source.

accepted.s: In which place was Jawaharlal Nehru’s ‘The Discovery of India’ written?
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote ‘The Discovery of India’ in Ahmednagar Fort jail.
accepted.tq: Test the place associated with a major work.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: A National Flag for India — Pingali
History of the Indian National Congress — Pattabhi
accepted.x: ‘Feathers and Stones’ was written by Pattabhi, not Sarojini Naidu. Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj, while Pingali wrote A National Flag for India in 1916.
accepted.tq: Catch the swapped author in a list of familiar works.

accepted.s: ‘Sarvodaya’ is best described as which of the following?
o: A Hindi translation by Nehru of ‘The Discovery of India’
A collection of Ambedkar’s speeches on caste
A Gujarati rendering by Gandhi of John Ruskin’s ‘Unto This Last’
A Tamil translation of Gandhi’s prison songs
accepted.x: Gandhi’s ‘Sarvodaya’ is a Gujarati rendering of John Ruskin’s ‘Unto This Last’.
accepted.tq: Test the exact nature and source of a translated work.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organisation)
a. Khaksars
b. Bal Charkha Sangh
c. Servants of the People Society
d. Independence for India League

List-II (Founder)
i. Jawaharlal Nehru
 ii. Indira Gandhi
 iii. Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi
 iv. Lala Lajpat Rai

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Khaksars were founded by Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi, Bal Charkha Sangh by Indira Gandhi, Servants of the People Society by Lala Lajpat Rai and the Independence for India League by Jawaharlal Nehru.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure founder–organisation pair and eliminate codes.

accepted.s: The Khaksars organisation was founded in which year?
accepted.x: Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi founded the Khaksars in 1931.
accepted.tq: Use nearby-year discrimination among organisations.

accepted.s: Which organisation was founded by Lala Lajpat Rai?
accepted.x: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society.
accepted.tq: Distinguish organisations with similar names by their founders.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded in 1932.
2. It had branches at Hyderabad and Vijayawada.
3. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was the president of its Vijayawada branch.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded in 1932 and had branches at Hyderabad and Vijayawada, whose Vijayawada branch was headed by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
accepted.tq: Combine date, location and office-holder facts in one coded question.

accepted.s: From which saint did Gandhi take the term ‘Harijan’?
accepted.x: Gandhi took the term ‘Harijan’ from the saint Narsi Mehta.
accepted.tq: Test the source of a distinctive political-social term.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Sarojini Naidu is correct?
1. She was associated with the Dharasana raid of 1930.
2. She became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
3. She was associated with Hyderabad.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Sarojini Naidu was associated with Hyderabad, the Dharasana raid of 1930 and became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Confirm a personality through region and multiple contributions.
accepted.sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Durgabai Deshmukh stopped Jawaharlal Nehru without a pass at which place and event?
accepted.x: Durgabai Deshmukh stopped Nehru without a pass at the Vijayawada AICC meeting in 1921.
accepted.tq: Link a freedom fighter with a distinctive incident, place and year.
accepted.sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali — Hoisting the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942
Bhikaiji Cama — Quit India martyrdom at Tamluk
Durgabai Deshmukh — Translation of Gandhi’s Hindi speeches into Telugu
accepted.x: Bhikaiji Cama was associated with hoisting the Indian flag abroad at Stuttgart in 1907. Matangini Hazra was the Quit India martyr associated with Tamluk.
accepted.tq: Reject the mismatched contribution by comparing regional associations.
accepted.sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rani Gaidinliu joined the Heraka movement at approximately what age?
accepted.x: Rani Gaidinliu joined the Zeliangrong Heraka movement at the age of 13 and was jailed for about 14 years.
accepted.tq: Test a distinctive biographical number.
accepted.sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who gave Rani Gaidinliu the title ‘Rani’?
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru called Gaidinliu ‘Rani’.
accepted.tq: Identify the person associated with a bestowed title.
accepted.sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Rani Velu Nachiyar wages war against the British
B. Bhikaiji Cama hoists the Indian flag at Stuttgart
C. Durgabai Deshmukh’s Vijayawada AICC incident
D. Aruna Asaf Ali hoists the flag at Gowalia Tank
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1780, 1907, 1921 and 1942: Rani Velu Nachiyar, Bhikaiji Cama, Durgabai Deshmukh and Aruna Asaf Ali.
accepted.tq: Arrange events by their stated years, using the earliest event first.
accepted.sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The statement, ‘Generations to come... will scarce believe that such a one... walked upon this earth’, was made by whom?
accepted.x: Albert Einstein made this statement in tribute to Mahatma Gandhi.
accepted.tq: Use quotation–speaker discrimination among prominent personalities.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gandhi described sedition as having become his religion.
2. Gandhi compared the Cripps offer to a post-dated cheque.
3. Subhas Chandra Bose compared the Dandi March with Napoleon’s return from Elba.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Gandhi made the first two observations, while Subhas Chandra Bose made the comparison concerning the Dandi March.
accepted.tq: Separate similar nationalist quotations by speaker and context.

accepted.s: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai founded which organisation?
accepted.x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin.
accepted.tq: Match a leader with the organisation founded by him.

accepted.s: The Coral Mill strike of 1908 was associated with V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and which other leader?
accepted.x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai participated in the 1908 Coral Mill strike along with Subramania Siva.
accepted.tq: Identify the associated co-participant in a specific movement.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: C. Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam Salt March. K. Kelappan was associated with Kerala, Gopinath Bordoloi with Assam and Kesari Singh Barahath with Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Use region–leader–movement association to eliminate mismatches.

accepted.s: Who was known as the ‘Kerala Gandhi’?
accepted.x: K. Kelappan of Kerala was popularly known as the ‘Kerala Gandhi’ and was associated with the Guruvayur Satyagraha.
accepted.tq: Test a regional honorific and its associated movement.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with Punjab.
2. He was a member of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.
3. He presided over the Indian National Congress in 1920.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Lala Lajpat Rai belonged to Punjab, formed part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio and presided over the Congress in 1920.
accepted.tq: Combine region, political association and office held.

accepted.s: Gopinath Bordoloi is best associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: Leader of the Guruvayur Satyagraha in Kerala
Poet and revolutionary of Shahpura in Rajasthan
Builder of modern Assam who was jailed in 1941 and 1942
Founder of the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in Tamil Nadu
accepted.x: Gopinath Bordoloi was regarded as a builder of modern Assam and was jailed in 1941 and 1942.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct regional biography from closely related alternatives.

accepted.s: Kesari Singh Barahath was associated with which region and role?
accepted.x: Kesari Singh Barahath belonged to Shahpura in Rajasthan and was known as a poet and revolutionary.
accepted.tq: Match region with identity and contribution.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes Subramania Siva?
1. He belonged to Tamil Nadu.
2. He was the first political prisoner of the Madras Presidency.
3. He worked with V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and Subramania Bharati.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Subramania Siva was from Tamil Nadu, regarded as the first political prisoner of the Madras Presidency, and worked with VOC and Bharati.
accepted.tq: Confirm a lesser-known personality through three linked facts.
